title: The cost page names each task and says once how many tokens have no price, on which models, and how to price them
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-postgres/src/cost.rs (the window's SQL: `total`, `models`, `missions`, `tasks`, `agents`, `executions`), crates/spawn-cli/src/cost.rs (prices, SPAWN_MODEL_PRICES), crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs (`cost`, `label_context`) and crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/labels.rs (a task's `label`, as `/api/missions` gives it), web/src/cost.ts (`costView`, `Row`) and web/src/components/cost/CostView.tsx.

The problem, as the owner reads the Cost page after 73e3596d (lead-mac, sync/queue.md 23:45; sync/page-cost-2026-11-11-2336.png).
- Every row is an id: "T251 $34.05", "agent_worker_objective_251 $34.05". Nothing on the page says what task 251 was, so "what did I pay $34 for" has no answer there.
- "unpriced use" badges sit on the 7-day total, on all four missions and on single tasks, with no word on which model is unpriced or how much. The owner cannot tell whether $1,778.71 is 1% or 50% low. Measured on the live `/api/cost?window=7d` at 15:4xZ: 2,128,602,277 of 5,576,854,833 tokens (38%) are on models with no price (deepseek-flash 1,812,108,660, deepseek-v4-pro 316,493,617). The answer's `models` rows carry no `unpriced_tokens`, while `total` and the missions do.

Required behaviour.
(a) `/api/cost`: every `models` row carries `unpriced_tokens` (its four counts when the model has no price, 0 when it has one). Every `tasks` row carries `label`, the task's label exactly as `/api/missions` gives it (serve/labels.rs), or null for a task the record does not hold.
(b) web/src/cost.ts: `costView(answer).unpriced_note` says once for the window how many tokens have no price, grouped "en-US" (`275,000`), on which models (named; a priced model is not named), and how to price them (SPAWN_MODEL_PRICES). It is null when every token is priced. Each `Row` carries `unpriced_tokens` (its count, 0 when none) and `label` (the API's label, or null).
(c) The Cost page shows the note under the window's total, in place of the bare "unpriced use" badge there. A row with unpriced use says its count ("+ 220,000 tokens unpriced"). A task row shows its label beside its id.
(d) cost.ts keeps loading with node alone (relative imports, `import type` only).

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/059.sh. A real `spawn loop` runs ephemeral workers of two missions on 048's fake engine, so the Bridge records each call's usage and cost, and `spawn serve` answers. bb-model-x is priced and bb-model-z is not. c1 (mission A) uses x for $0.45 and z for 220,000 tokens; c2 (mission B) uses z for 55,000. Checks:
- (1) The 24 h answer's `models` rows carry `unpriced_tokens`: x 0, z 275000.
- (4) Task c1's row carries `label` equal to `/api/missions`'s.
- Under node, `costView` over that answer:
  - (2) `unpriced_note` names 275,000, bb-model-z (not bb-model-x) and SPAWN_MODEL_PRICES, and is null for a fully priced answer;
  - (3) the mission rows' `unpriced_tokens` are 220000 and 55000;
  - (4) c1's task row's `label` is the API's.
It fails with 1 on 73e3596d at (1), (4) and the page checks.

The product reason. Cost is where the owner decides what the fleet may spend. A total that is silently 38% low, and rows nobody can name, make that decision blind. The note says once how big the gap is and how to close it, and the labels say what each dollar bought.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour: a spawn-postgres test of the models rows through the real store, a serve test of the task label, and web/test tests for (b) and (c).
